note: Frozen before the main STEP 5-2 extraction. The evaluation must use this preregistration; a change requires a new version with a recorded reason.

revision.reason: The v1 integrity check required the N image's features in N-first inputs to match across image counts within atol/rtol 1e-5. The pilot (64 records, no evaluation metric computed) showed differences up to 1.28 (absolute). Diagnosis: the bf16 vision encoder gives slightly different embeddings for the same image depending on the other images processed with it (relative L2 0.4-7%); with the vision encoder in float32 the difference is 4e-7 to 1e-5, so this is numerical error, not information flowing between images. In LLM features the gap was cosine distance <= 3.4e-4 and relative L2 <= 2.6%; frozen z_i probe p(P) changed by <= 0.04. The same effect exists in STEP 1-4 (STEP 3/4 merge context vectors within cosine distance 0.001).
changes: Integrity criterion for N-first identity: cosine distance <= 0.001 at every layer (was atol/rtol 1e-5).
Inputs above the criterion are listed and a sensitivity analysis excluding them is added.
Reported with the criterion: relative L2 and frozen z_i probe p(P) changes; exploratory: signed mean z_N change by image count in N-first.
New sensitivity analysis: vision encoder in float32 on a seeded subset, comparing P4 - P1.
Interpretation wording: N's representation in N-first is identical within bf16 numerical error (bound stated).
Run metadata records the language-model dtype and the vision dtype; model loading gains an optional float32 vision encoder (default unchanged).
revision.unchanged: hypotheses, cases, outcomes, minimum effects, decision rules, statistics
revision.pilot_policy: As in STEP 4, the pilot (results/step5/.../accumulation/pilot, 64 records, run under v1) is an integrity check only and is not part of any analysis. The main extraction re-runs every frozen case, including the 64 pilot cases, and only the full main run is evaluated.

hypotheses.H0: Minimum / Product-AND over fixed per-image evidence: adding P images to an input that keeps the same N image does not increase the Yes margin or the False-Yes rate.
hypotheses.H1: Positive Evidence Accumulation: adding P images increases the Yes margin and the False-Yes rate.
hypotheses.H2: Secondary: for the same N image, placement and image count, the High-P series gives a higher False-Yes rate and margin than the Low-P series (same image counts, different evidence strength).
hypotheses.caveat: H0's prediction assumes that the evidence of the existing images and the decision criterion stay fixed. An increase is reported as a disagreement with fixed-evidence AND models, not as a rejection of every AND computation.

preregistration.unit: N image (anchor). Each N image has one High and one Low series of five P images; analyses pair inputs within a series.

definitions.answer_parsing: Greedy generation, max_new_tokens 8. The decoded response is stripped of surrounding whitespace, then of trailing '.', '!', '?', stripped again and case-folded; 'yes' -> Yes, 'no' -> No, anything else -> unparsed.
definitions.false_yes: ground truth No (one-N input) and parsed answer Yes; unparsed answers are not Yes and are counted separately
definitions.yes_rate_all_positive: share of All-P inputs whose parsed answer is Yes (unparsed counted as not Yes)
definitions.margin_primary: fp32 variant margin: logsumexp over the answer-variant token logits for Yes minus that for No, with logits computed in float64 arithmetic from the bf16 final-layer (after norm) last-input-token state and the bf16 output-embedding rows. Variant token sets are the single tokens that equal yes / no after stripping whitespace and case-folding; the exact lists are recorded in run.json. Field: fp32_variant_logit_margin.
definitions.margin_sensitivity: bf16 generation logits of the capitalized 'Yes' and 'No' tokens (STEP 1-4 definition). Field: logit_margin.

primary.contrast: P = 4 minus P = 1 within the same series (same N image, same strength, same placement), averaged over series
primary.trend: secondary: least-squares slope of the False-Yes rate over P = 1..4

co_primary_margin.outcome: primary margin (fp32 variant) on one-N inputs
co_primary_margin.contrast: P = 4 minus P = 1 within series, by placement

minimum_effect.confirmed_by: user, before any STEP 5-2 model output
minimum_effect.rationale: STEP 5-1 (exploratory): top vs bottom tercile of mean P evidence differed by +0.156 in False-Yes rate and +0.59 in margin; +1 SD of P evidence went with +0.31 margin. The STEP 4 one-N False-Yes rate was 0.274. 0.05 is about one third of the tercile contrast and 18% of the baseline rate; 0.25 logit is two bf16 margin steps (0.125), 0.22 SD of the STEP 4 margin and close to the +1 SD association. 5-1 measured mean P evidence, 5-2 varies the number of P images, so these are practical lower bounds rather than predictions.

decision.per_placement_supported: point estimate >= minimum effect AND N-image cluster bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0
decision.robust_label: A supported placement is labelled 'robust support' only if the class-level cluster bootstrap 95% CI lower bound is also > 0; otherwise 'support (cross-class generalization uncertain)'.
decision.per_placement_no_meaningful_increase: N-image cluster bootstrap 95% CI upper bound < minimum effect
decision.H1_supported: False-Yes rule met in both N-first and N-last (the margin is reported with the same rule as co-primary)
decision.one_placement_only: Report placement-specific alternatives with the exploratory results: N-first = distance between N and the question grows; N-last = the N representation can change with preceding P images.
decision.no_increase: Do not extend the STEP 5-1 association to a causal aggregation effect.

control.all_positive: Yes rate and margin of All-P inputs with the same image count and placement (N slot filled with the next series image), reported next to the one-N False-Yes rate.
control.difference_in_differences: Secondary, not part of the decision: (one-N primary-margin change P4 - P1) - (All-P primary-margin change between the same image counts, 2 -> 5 images), within series and placement.

secondary.H2_high_minus_low: Paired High - Low within the same N image, placement and image count, for the False-Yes rate and the primary margin. Reported for each image count (2-5) and pooled (mean over counts), by placement, with N-image cluster CIs. Also reported: whether High - Low grows with the P count (slope over P = 1..4).
secondary.trend: least-squares slope over P = 1..4 for the False-Yes rate and the primary margin
secondary.margin_sensitivity: all primary and H2 contrasts repeated with the bf16 'Yes'/'No' margin
secondary.sign_consistency: contrasts repeated without inputs whose bf16 margin sign disagrees with the answer (ties included)
secondary.integrity_exclusion: contrasts repeated without the N-first inputs whose N features exceed cosine distance 0.001 against the series' two-image input (listed in n_first_exceeding_inputs.json), together with the paired inputs they belong to
secondary.vision_fp32: Seeded subset: 6 N images per class (120 N images, 240 series), all one-N inputs (P = 1..4, both placements, both strengths; 1,920 records), re-run with the vision encoder in float32 (language model unchanged, bf16). Compared with the main bf16 run on the same series: direction and size of P4 - P1 for the False-Yes rate and the primary margin, and their paired difference with N-image cluster CIs. Selection never uses outcomes.

interpretation.n_first_representation: In N-first inputs the N image's representation is identical within bf16 numerical error: cosine distance <= 0.001 at every layer against the same series' two-image input (pilot: <= 3.4e-4, relative L2 <= 2.6%, |delta p(P)| <= 0.04); the full-run range is reported with the results.

model_predictions.note: Qualitative predictions written before the data. P effect = one-N change P4 - P1; DiD as defined above.

rows.model: AND over fixed per-image evidence (Minimum / Product)

rows.high_minus_low: present and grows with the P count

rows.model: Mean over all images (N share diluted)
General Yes tendency with image count

exploratory: Per-class P effects (P4 - P1) for the False-Yes rate and the primary margin
N-first: signed mean change of the N image's frozen z_i probe score (logit and p(P), each layer) by image count, against the two-image input
N-last: change of z_N (frozen STEP 4 z_i probe, L36) with image count
h_q readouts only where the N image sits at positions 1-3 (readouts exist for positions 1-3 only; off-distribution)

statistics.resampling_unit: N image ID (anchor); all series and inputs of a drawn N image enter together
statistics.sensitivity: class-level cluster bootstrap (P images are reused across N images only within a class); used for the robust label

integrity_checks: Token count of each image identical across all inputs that contain it
N-first: the N image's features identical across image counts within bf16 numerical error (cosine distance <= 0.001 at every layer), since it sees no later image
Agreement rate between margin sign and generated answer (bf16 and primary margin)

pilot.policy: As in STEP 4, the pilot (results/step5/.../accumulation/pilot, 64 records, run under v1) is an integrity check only and is not part of any analysis. The main extraction re-runs every frozen case, including the 64 pilot cases, and only the full main run is evaluated.
